[CBSE Class X Science, sample question paper, 2026-27]
25. Carbon forms millions of compounds whereas silicon, which is just below it in 2
the Periodic Table, forms a few compounds. Explain the reason for the
difference in their ability to form compounds.

[CBSE Class X Science, marking scheme, 2026-27]
25. Carbon forms millions of compounds because it has small atomic size, 2
therefore, it forms strong and stable C–C bonds, showing extensive
catenation. Silicon, being larger in size, forms weaker Si–Si bonds and
cannot show catenation to the same extent, so it forms fewer compounds.
